stem: Derive the expression for the maximum work.

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem: Obtain the relatioship between \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta U\) for gas phase reactions.
State Hess's law of constant heat summation. Illustrate with an example. State its applications.

Although \(\Delta S\) for the formation of two moles of water from \(\mathrm{H_2}\) and \(\mathrm{O_2}\) is \(-327\ \mathrm{JK^{-1}}\), it is spontaneous. Explain. (Given \(\Delta H\) for the reaction is \(-572\) kJ).
Obtain the relation between \(\Delta G\) and \(\Delta S_{total}\). Comment on spontaneity of the reaction.

One mole of an ideal gas is compressed from 500 \(\mathrm{cm^3}\) against a constant external pressure of \(1.2 \times 10^5\) Pa. The work involved in the process is 36.0 J. Calculate the final volume.
Calculate the maximum work when 24 g of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) are expanded isothermally and reversibly from the pressure of 1.6 bar to 1 bar at 298 K.

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem:
Calculate the work done in the decomposition of 132 g of \(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}\) at \(100^\circ\mathrm{C}\).
\(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3(s) \longrightarrow N_2O(g) + 2\,H_2O(g)}\)
State whether work is done on the system or by the system.

Calculate standard enthalpy of reaction,
\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 3CO(g) \longrightarrow 2\,Fe(s) + 3CO_2(g)}\),
from the following data.
\(\Delta_f H^0(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}) = -824\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\),
\(\Delta_f H^0(\mathrm{CO}) = -110\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\),
\(\Delta_f H^0(\mathrm{CO_2}) = -393\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\)
For a certain reaction \(\Delta H^0 = 219\ \mathrm{kJ}\) and \(\Delta S^0 = -21\ \mathrm{J/K}\). Determine whether the reaction is spontaneous or nonspontaneous.

Determine whether the following reaction is spontaneous under standard state conditions.
\(\mathrm{2\,H_2O(\mathit{l}) + O_2(g) \longrightarrow 2H_2O_2(\mathit{l})}\)
if \(\Delta H^0 = 196\ \mathrm{kJ}\), \(\Delta S^0 = -126\ \mathrm{J/K}\)
Does it have a cross-over temperature?

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem:
Calculate \(\Delta U\) at 298 K for the reaction,
\(\mathrm{C_2H_4(g) + HCl(g) \longrightarrow C_2H_5Cl(g)}\), \(\Delta H = -72.3\ \mathrm{kJ}\)
How much \(PV\) work is done?

Calculate the work done during synthesis of \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) in which volume changes from 8.0 \(\mathrm{dm^3}\) to 4.0 \(\mathrm{dm^3}\) at a constant external pressure of 43 bar. In what direction the work energy flows?
bookAnswer: Ans. : (17.2 kJ, work energy flows into system)

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem:
Calculate the amount of work done in the
(a) oxidation of 1 mole HCl(g) at \(200^\circ\mathrm{C}\) according to reaction.
\(\mathrm{4HCl(g) + O_2(g) \longrightarrow 2\,Cl_2(g) + 2\,H_2O(g)}\)
(b) decomposition of one mole of NO at \(300^\circ\mathrm{C}\) for the reaction
\(\mathrm{2\,NO(g) \longrightarrow N_2(g) + O_2}\)

When 6.0 g of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) reacts with CIF as per
\(\mathrm{2Cl\,F(g) + O_2(g) \longrightarrow Cl_2O(g) + OF_2(g)}\)
The enthalpy change is 38.55 kJ. What is standard enthalpy of the reaction ?

Calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of \(\mathrm{CH_3OH(\mathit{l})}\) from the following data
i. \(\mathrm{CH_3OH(\mathit{l}) + \tfrac{3}{2}\,O_2(g) \longrightarrow CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(\mathit{l})}\), \(\Delta H^0 = -726\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)
ii. \(\mathrm{C\,(Graphite) + O_2(g) \longrightarrow CO_2(g)}\), \(\Delta_c H^0 = -393\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)
iii. \(\mathrm{H_2(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}\,O_2(g) \longrightarrow H_2O(\mathit{l})}\), \(\Delta_f H^0 = -286\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)

Calculate \(\Delta H^0\) for the following reaction at 298 K
\(\mathrm{H_2B_4O_7(s) + H_2O(\mathit{l}) \longrightarrow 4HBO_2\,(aq)}\)
i. \(\mathrm{2H_3BO_3(aq) \longrightarrow B_2O_3(s) + 3H_2O(\mathit{l})}\), \(\Delta H^0 = 14.4\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)
ii. \(\mathrm{H_3BO_3(aq) \longrightarrow HBO_2(aq) + H_2O,(\mathit{l})}\), \(\Delta H^0 = -0.02\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)
iii. \(\mathrm{H_2B_4O_7(s) \longrightarrow 2P_2O_3(s) + H_2O(\mathit{l})}\), \(\Delta H^0 = 17.3\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem: Calculate the total heat required (a) to melt 180 g of ice at \(0^\circ\mathrm{C}\), (b) heat it to \(100^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and then (c) vapourise it at that temperature. Given \(\Delta_{fus}H^0(\mathrm{ice}) = 6.01\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) at \(0^\circ\mathrm{C}\), \(\Delta_{vap}H^0(\mathrm{H_2O}) = 40.7\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) at \(100^\circ\mathrm{C}\) specific heat of water is \(4.18\ \mathrm{J\ g^{-1}\ K^{-1}}\)

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem:
The enthalpy change for the reaction,
\(\mathrm{C_2H_4(g) + H_2(g) \longrightarrow C_2H_6(g)}\)
is \(-620\) J when 100 ml of ethylene and 100 mL of \(\mathrm{H_2}\) react at 1 bar pressure. Calculate the pressure volume type of work and \(\Delta U\) for the reaction.

subtopic: Enthalpy and Enthalpies of Physical Transformations
stem:
Calculate the work done and comment on whether work is done on or by the system for the decomposition of 2 moles of \(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}\) at \(100^\circ\mathrm{C}\)
\(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3(s) \longrightarrow N_2O(g) + 2H_2O(g)}\)
bookAnswer: Ans. (-18.61 kJ, work is done by the system)
